text:
alex: Quick follow-up on the on-prem upgrade RFC — I sketched a manifest-driven, CAS-backed delta delivery approach for air-gapped installs. Main open questions: how do we guarantee atomicity across service binaries + DB schema changes? Also key-rotation for signed manifests? Thoughts?

maria: +1 on CAS for bandwidth. For atomicity we should split into two phases: download+verify artifacts, then run migrations, then switch symlink / update images. A health-check gating step between migrations and switch is critical.

kevin: Leader election is tricky for single-node appliances. We should support an explicit "migration-runner" CLI mode so an operator can run migrations manually with a --confirm flag. Automating migrations by default feels risky.

sophie: For k8s private deployments: use a Job to run migrations, block Deployment rollout via PodDisruptionBudget + readiness probe until migrations succeed. For systemd installs use dual-release dirs (/opt/redwood/releases/<id>) and an atomic symlink swap.

alex: Good. Rollback semantics? Keep N=2 releases by default and only allow automatic rollback if migrations were no-op or reversible. If migration made destructive schema changes, require manual intervention.

maria: Also add a "compatibility" block in the manifest that lists supported DB major/minor versions and marks non-reversible migrations as "breaking: true". The verifier should refuse auto-rollback for breaking releases.

kevin: Security point: manifests signed by vendor and optionally re-signed by customer KMS. Key-rotation: new signing keys are allowed immediately for new manifests, but old key must remain valid for verifying older manifests until those releases expire. Need guidance from security on rotation TTLs. @security

sophie: We should ship a small offline verifier binary that runs entirely local: checks signatures, verifies checksums, validates manifest schema, and runs a dry-run of migration checks (e.g., check for missing tables/columns). This helps ops validate before applying.

alex: Example manifest sketch (very small):
```
version: 1
release_id: r2026-03-15
artifacts:
  - path: server.tar.gz
    sha256: abc123...
  - path: migrations.sql
    sha256: def456...
migrations:
  order: [migrations.sql]
  breaking: [schema_remove_old_table]
compatibility:
  min_db: 12.5
  max_db: 13.x
signatures:
  vendor: sig1_base64
  customer: sig2_base64
```

maria: Consider chunked binary deltas to avoid shipping full tarballs for small changes. That reduces airtime but increases complexity in patcher and verification. If we do chunk deltas, include per-chunk checksums and a final manifest checksum.

kevin: Ops/observability: add upgrade metrics — bytes_transferred, verify_duration_ms, migration_duration_ms, checksum_failures, rollback_count. Expose to local Prometheus and write a short upgrade log that operators can send to support.

alex: Action items: I'll update the RFC to include: leader-election fallback/manual-runner, manifest schema additions (compatibility, breaking flags, signatures metadata), offline verifier tool, rollback policy (keep last 2, block auto-rollback on breaking migrations), and metrics. I'll follow up with @infra and @security for key-rotation TTLs and storage recommendations.

deploy-bot: New build r2026-03-15-candidate uploaded to s3-mirror (sha256 abc123...). :rocket:
